inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL us-gaap:ShareBasedCompensation, FY2025 10-K cash-flow add-back $49.0M (H1-2026 $41M, i.e. ~0.47% of revenue annualised after AssuredPartners awards). No combined 'SBC incl. equity-award taxes' figure and no PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation tag is filed; withholding is immaterial at this SBC intensity. Forward path is set at 0.45% of revenue to reflect the post-deal H1-2026 run-rate rather than the FY2025 0.35%.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 256.3M basic shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (10-Q cover/balance sheet, CommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~3.0M dilutive options/units, cross-checked to H1-2026 net income / diluted EPS (1,146 / 4.41 = 259.9M weighted diluted). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The FY2024-25 rise from 216.7M to 257M was the AssuredPartners equity raise (genuine non-SBC issuance), already inside the base count; no further issuance is modelled. AJG is currently a repurchaser ($480M bought back in H1-2026), so the flat count is funded, not just a convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 8.0%, single rate across all three scenarios (risk is carried in the bear flows, not stacked into the discount rate). USD flows: 10yr UST ~4.3%, ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~0.8 for a fee-based broker (historically 0.7-0.8) -> cost of equity ~8.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.2% (senior notes) -> ~4.0% after tax at a ~19% debt weight on market values (13.6bn debt vs ~59bn equity). Arithmetic WACC ~7.5%; rounded up to 8.0% for post-AssuredPartners leverage (~3x net debt/EBITDA) and integration execution risk.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A: ASC 842 operating leases (FY2025 lease cost $197M, liability $646M). Operating-lease cost is inside GAAP opex, so it is already charged in the EBITDA margin; the lease liability is NOT added to net debt. D&A (DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet) excludes operating-lease ROU amortisation, so there is no double charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is $30M of book equity (2026-06-30) and $1M of H1-2026 earnings -- deducted once in the equity bridge at book; flows are consolidated.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (routing table row 1/2: operating company). AJG is an insurance BROKER, not an insurer: it places risk with third-party carriers for commissions/fees (Brokerage ~89%) and runs third-party claims administration (Gallagher Bassett, ~11%). It carries no underwriting risk, so the BVPS/insurer route does not apply. Fiduciary cash and premiums payable (~$8bn of cash in the fiduciary-inclusive total at 2026-06-30) belong to clients/carriers and are excluded from cash; the investment income earned on them is recurring operating revenue and stays in revenue (not stripped as interest income). ANCHORS: price 2026-09-24 close; balance sheet 2026-06-30 10-Q. Total debt $13,609M = DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount (11,955 long-term + 1,520 short-term borrowings under the credit facility + current portion) -- the prior Sonnet build used only the 11,955 non-current line and missed ~$1.65bn (~$6.4/share). Cash $1,137M = non-fiduciary cash & equivalents (1,386 incl. restricted) less $249M restricted cash. REVENUE BASE AND THE M&A QUESTION: FY2025 revenue (13,942) holds AssuredPartners (closed 2025-08-18) for only 4.5 months and includes interest on ~$13bn of pre-close deal funds held Jan-Aug 2025. Year 1 (FY2026E ~16.6bn, +19.4%) is built bottom-up: H1-2026 actual 8,761 + H2 estimate ~7,880 (H2-2025 x ~6% organic, plus AP's missing ~1.5 months, plus tuck-ins already closed, less the non-repeating escrow interest). From Year 2 onward growth is ORGANIC ONLY. AJG buys ~$1-2bn of brokers a year (77 deals in H1-2026); modelling that inorganic growth without charging the acquisition cash would be free growth, and charging it via capex would need a return assumption we cannot anchor. The tuck-in program is therefore treated as NPV-neutral -- a deliberate conservatism; if AJG keeps buying at ~10-12x EBITDA and extracting its historical synergies, that is upside not in any scenario. MARGIN: EBITDA margin here is GAAP EBITDA before SBC (pretax + interest + D&A + SBC), NOT AJG's 'adjusted EBITDAC' (Brokerage 33.6-34.2% guided), because it must carry integration costs, earnout remeasurements, corporate-segment costs and Risk Management's lower margin. TTM to 2026-06-30 it was ~25.6%, H1-2026 28.8% (Q1 is the seasonal peak), H2-2025 21.6% (heavy AP deal/integration costs). Base ramps 26.5% (FY2026) to a mature 30.0% by Year 6 as integration spend rolls off and the $325M run-rate AP synergies (~1.8pp of revenue) land. D&A: FY2026 ~8.0% of revenue (intangible amortisation schedule 1,105 / 1,071 / 1,028 / 973 / 917 for 2026-30, plus ~1.5% depreciation); because no new acquisitions are modelled the acquired-intangible amortisation runs off, so D&A tapers to 1.1% in Year 10 = capex, so the terminal year does not perpetuate an amortisation tax shield. This taper is faster than the actual schedule ($5.6bn of amortisation remains after 2030), which slightly understates the tax shield -- conservative. CAPEX: 1.1% of revenue (FY2025 $145M = 1.0%, H1-2026 $87M = 1.0%). CASH TAX: 24% of EBIT, flat -- US federal+state blended with UK/Australia at 25-30%; FY2025 book ETR 19.7% includes ~1pp of clean-energy credit benefit and the levered interest shield. The remaining Section 45 clean-coal tax credit carryforward ($628M DTA at 2026-06-30, being consumed at ~$170M/yr) is valued once, in the equity bridge, not in the tax rate. WORKING CAPITAL: 0% capture -- non-fiduciary working capital is small and does not scale with growth; fiduciary timing swings OCF quarter-to-quarter but nets to zero. HORIZON: 10 years; margin matures Year 6, amortisation runs off by Year 10.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: organic_growth_guidance (FY2026 ~6% total organic, Brokerage ~5% after the Sept-2026 cut, Risk Management 9-12%); no historical CAGR is an organic series
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (36.4% 3yr / 30.2% 5yr) diverges >30% from revenue (17.7%/14.8%) and EPS (3.4%/6.4%): book value was inflated by ~$10bn of new equity raised for AssuredPartners, not by retained earnings. Revenue CAGR is acquisition-driven (tuck-ins plus AP). Owner-FCF CAGR is 0.5% over 5 years because FY2020 OCF ($1.81bn) was flattered by COVID-era working capital and FY2025 ($1.93bn) was depressed by AP transaction/integration cash and $491M of earnout settlements.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = OCF - capex (PaymentsForCapitalImprovements) - SBC: FY2020 1,694; FY2022 1,183; FY2025 1,736 ($M). SBC-adjusted and reported FCF CAGRs are close (SBC is ~0.35% of revenue), so SBC is not eating the growth. Forward growth is anchored on organic guidance, not on any of these CAGRs.

base.narrative: Guidance delivered, then a mid-single-digit organic broker.

bear.narrative: Soft property cycle drags on; integration gains are competed away.

scenario_narratives.base: AJG meets its cut FY2026 guide (Brokerage organic ~5%, Gallagher Bassett 9-12%, ~6% blended) and then grows organically at 4-5% a year -- exposure-unit growth plus modest rate, with property renewal pricing (down ~10% in Q2-2026) weighing while casualty and professional lines stay firm. AssuredPartners integration runs on plan: $160M run-rate synergies by end-2026 and $325M by early 2028, and integration spend rolls off, lifting the GAAP EBITDA margin from ~26.5% to ~30% by Year 6. Tuck-in M&A continues but is valued at zero NPV.
scenario_narratives.bull: The softening is confined to property and brief; casualty/social-inflation, cyber and benefits complexity keep advisory demand and premium inflation high, so Brokerage organic returns to 6-7% and Gallagher Bassett keeps compounding at double digits. AP synergies beat the $325M target and the shared-services centres keep adding 40-60bps a year, taking the margin to ~31.5% -- close to AJG's guided Brokerage adjusted EBITDAC once corporate costs are absorbed.
scenario_narratives.bear: The P&C cycle turns fully soft for several years (property rates keep falling and casualty follows), contingent/supplemental commissions tied to carrier profitability compress, and AI-driven placement and embedded distribution erode small-commercial fees. Brokerage organic sinks to 2-3% (as in the 2015-17 soft market), AP integration slips and the synergies are reinvested to retain producers, so the margin stalls near 27%. Leverage (~3x) limits buybacks and the M&A engine slows.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 20% (above the 15% default): the P&C pricing cycle is visibly softening, management has just cut the FY2026 organic guide, and the largest integration in AJG's history is only a year in. Base 55%: guidance, synergy targets and the amortisation schedule give a well-anchored central path. Bull 25% (below the 35% default): it needs both a quick end to the property softening and synergy over-delivery.

valuation_philosophy.summary: AJG is valued as an asset-light fee business on an owner-FCF basis with ORGANIC growth only after FY2026; the tuck-in acquisition machine is treated as NPV-neutral rather than as free growth. Debt is the full 2026-06-30 combined debt including credit-facility borrowings; fiduciary cash is excluded; the remaining clean-energy tax credits and estimated earnout payables sit in the equity bridge.
key_risks_to_valuation: Earnout payables are an estimate ($600M) -- each $260M is ~$1/share
Organic growth sensitivity to a prolonged soft P&C pricing cycle
GAAP EBITDA margin path depends on AssuredPartners integration costs rolling off and $325M synergies landing
Excluding M&A value understates AJG if its tuck-ins keep earning above WACC -- the main source of upside not in the model
Cash tax 24% on EBIT is a judgment; each 1pp is roughly $2/share
